title: Hensheng: To Hate Life 6
content:
Jiang-zongzhu always laced his words with a sharp edge of mockery, but this time, the venom was aimed entirely at himself.

Suddenly, he rasped, "I'm sorry."

Wei Wuxian froze. "...You don't need to apologize."

At this point, who owed what to whom was a ledger far too tangled to ever balance.

Wei Wuxian added quietly, "Just consider it my way of paying back the Jiang Clan."

Jiang Cheng lifted his face. His eyes were a ruin of broken vessels, staring back with raw, inflamed rims. "Paying back?" he croaked. "Paying back my father? My mother? My sister?"

Wei Wuxian pressed his fingers hard against his throbbing temple. "Forget it. It’s all in the past. Let’s just drop it."

It wasn't a memory he took any pleasure in dragging out into the light. He had no desire to relive the sheer agony of being strapped down fully conscious while his golden core was sliced out, nor did he want to keep dwelling on the exact magnitude of the debt, or the price he’d paid for it.

If this truth had been torn open in his past life, he probably would have laughed it off with an easy wave, turning around to brush it away: Look, it really wasn't a big deal! See? I've been doing great all these years without that little core. Whoever crossed me got beaten bloody, and whoever made me mad ended up dead. But right now, he simply didn't have the energy left to put on that breezy, devil-may-care act.

Truth be told, he was never that detached to begin with.

How could anyone ever just shrug off something like that?

It was impossible.

Back when he was seventeen or eighteen, Wei Wuxian had been every bit as proud and fiercely competitive as Jiang Cheng. He’d had power, genius, and a boundless reserve of spiritual energy. He had spent his days skipping lessons to catch loaches, shooting kites, and scaling walls to pull all-nighters, yet he had effortlessly outpaced every single disciple in the sect who broke their backs trying to catch up with him.

Yet on those suffocating, sleepless nights, tossing and turning in the dark, the crushing weight of reality would claw at his throat: he would never again reach the peak of orthodox cultivation, never again draw that dazzling, showstopping blade that had once left the entire world speechless. Whenever that dark spiral dragged him under, he would force himself to flip the coin: if Jiang Fengmian had never plucked him off the cold streets and brought him home to Lotus Pier, he would have lived and died without ever brushing against the immortal path. He would never have known the magnificent wonders this world had to offer. He’d have spent his miserable days as a shivering beggar running from stray curs, or a peasant boy tending water buffalo, nicking wild vegetables, blowing on a makeshift bamboo flute to kill time. He would never have cultivated a single breath, let alone formed a golden core of his own.

Clinging to that thought had been the only thing that made the ache bearable.

Call it repayment. Call it penance. Just pretend that core was never mine to begin with.

Tell yourself a lie enough times, and you start wearing it like a second skin. He had managed to act every bit as cavalier as the world thought he was, even secretly patting himself on the back for being such a noble, high-minded soul.

Except that was a lifetime ago.

"Look," Wei Wuxian offered awkwardly, "try not to keep dwelling on it. I mean, knowing you, you’ll probably obsess over it forever, but... how should I put this..."

He laced his fingers tighter through Lan Wangji’s, looking Jiang Cheng dead in the eye. "Right now, I honestly feel like... it's over. It's been too long. There's really no point in hashing it out anymore."

Jiang Cheng scrubbed violently at his face with a sleeve, wiping away the tears. He pulled in a shaky breath, shut his eyes, and went silent.

Just then, Nie Huaisang—still swathed under the heavy folds of Lan Xichen’s outer robe—finally stirred back to consciousness. He let out a series of pitiful whimpers, weakly hauling himself upright on wobbly limbs, blinking blearily through the shadows. "Where... where am I?"

The moment his vision focused, the first sight that greeted him was Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji practically glued together on a single prayer mat, the infamous Yiling Laozu all but perched right in Hanguang-jun's lap. Nie Huaisang let out a bloodcurdling shriek, looking ready to pass right back out on the spot.

Before he could hit the floor, a sharp, unnatural hiss erupted from the rear of the main hall, like high-pressure steam violently bursting through stone. A split second later, a chorus of agonizing shrieks tore out from the digging crew behind the altar.

The air in the temple instantly curdled. A faint, acrid reek drifted into the room. Lan Xichen raised his sleeve to mask his face, a flicker of genuine alarm crossing his brow.

Two figures burst through the partition, staggering wildly into the light.

Su She had his arm looped under Jin Guangyao’s shoulder, both of them chalk-pale, while the hollow screams of the dying continued to reverberate from the back of the hall. "Sect Leader, how bad is it?!" Su She wheezed in a panic.

Cold beads of sweat stood out on Jin Guangyao’s forehead. "I'm fine," he forced out. "It's lucky you reacted in time."

His left arm hung limp and useless at his side, trembling violently as though every nerve were on fire. With his good right hand, he fished a small porcelain bottle from his inner lapel, struggling awkwardly to pop the cork one-handed. Seeing him fumble, Su She hastily took the vial, tipping a dark pill onto his palm. Jin Guangyao tossed it into his mouth and swallowed hard, the sharp scowl on his forehead smoothing out almost instantly.

Lan Xichen hesitated for a heartbeat before stepping forward, unable to completely choke down his concern. "What happened to you?"

Jin Guangyao blinked, a faint flush of color dragging itself back to his cheeks. He offered a strained, brittle smile. "A moment of carelessness, that is all."

He tapped a dusting of medicinal powder over his wounds. From the back of his left hand straight up to the wrist, the skin had blackened into an angry, blistered crimson. Looking closely, the flesh was completely corroded, ruptured and peeling away like meat pulled fresh from boiling oil. Ripping a strip of clean white cloth from his undergarments with trembling fingers, Jin Guangyao murmured, "Minshan. Bind my wrist. Tight."

Su She's eyes widened. "Poison?"

"The fumes are seeping up the veins," Jin Guangyao replied, keeping his voice dead even. "It will not kill me. A moment of meditation will be enough to force it out."

Once the dressing was secured, Jin Guangyao made a move toward the partition to survey the damage, but Su She immediately blocked his path. "Sect Leader, let me go instead!"

As the pungent, chemical stench gradually thinned out, Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji rose to their feet, trailing behind them.

Beyond the partition, a massive mountain of freshly excavated dirt was piled beside a cavernous trench. Tilted precariously against the edge of the pit sat an exquisitely lacquered coffin, draped beneath a heavy, pitch-black iron coffer. Both lids had been forced wide, thin ribbons of wispy white vapor still curling lazily into the damp air. That foul, nose-burning odor was coming from those very fumes—a lethally concentrated contact venom.

Scattered haphazardly around the coffin were the contorted remains of the cultivators who had been digging just moments before. They had already liquefied into gruesome, melted husks, their golden peony robes and plain Buddhist cassocks eaten away until only scorched, sodden rags clung to their rotting skin. The sheer toxicity of the mist was terrifying.

Su She charged ahead, sweeping the lingering vapor aside with a concentrated blast of sword glare, using the bare tip of his blade to flip the black iron box over.

The heavy trunk crashed into the dirt, entirely empty.

Jin Guangyao couldn't hold back anymore. He lurched forward, practically throwing himself against the lip of the open coffin. Whatever faint color had returned to his face vanished in an instant, draining into a sickly, corpse-like gray. Looking at his hollow expression, everyone in the hall knew without asking: the coffin was just as empty.

Lan Xichen followed closely behind. Taking in the gruesome butchery, shock broke through his composure: "What in heaven's name did you bury down here?! How could it come to this?!"

Nie Huaisang took one single look over his shoulder and dropped straight to his knees, dry-heaving violently onto the floorboards.

Jin Guangyao’s lips trembled, utterly robbed of words. A jagged bolt of lightning split the night sky, throwing his features into harsh, ghostly relief. The expression twisting his face was so feral, so utterly venomous, that Nie Huaisang shuddered to his core, swallowing down his retching and shrinking behind Lan Xichen like a terrified turtle, shivering uncontrollably from the chill—or the sheer horror.

Lan Xichen murmured a few quiet words to steady the shaking man, while Jin Guangyao stood frozen, clearly stripped of every ounce of energy required to keep up his usual smooth, amiable mask.

Wei Wuxian’s voice cut through the damp gloom: "Zewu-jun, you're blaming the wrong man here. Whatever was down in that dirt, Sect Leader Jin definitely didn't plant it there. Or rather, whatever he did bury... was swapped out behind his back a long time ago."

Su She whipped his sword around, leveling the steel straight at Wei Wuxian's throat. "Wei Wuxian! Are you the one playing tricks here?!"

Wei Wuxian chuckled dryly. "Not to brag, but if I were the one calling the shots behind that trap, your precious Sect Leader wouldn't have walked away with just a blistered arm. Jin-zongzhu, tell me: do you still remember that private letter Qin Su delivered straight to your hands back at Koi Tower?"

Jin Guangyao's cold, glassy gaze slowly drifted up to meet his.

Wei Wuxian pressed on, letting every syllable sink in: "The person who spilled the truth about your dirty laundry to Qin Su was her mother’s old maid, Bicao. But do you honestly believe that timid woman decided to step forward and blow the whistle entirely on her own? And what about that courtesan, Sisi, whom you had locked away in secret for over a decade? Who broke her out of that gilded cage? Who coached her and Bicao to march into Lotus Pier and tear your pristine reputation to shreds in front of every prominent sect in the realm?

"If that shadow had the resources to dig up your darkest, most tightly guarded skeletons, doesn't it make complete sense that they'd slip in here ahead of you, swap out your prized treasure for an explosive chest of contact poison, and sit back waiting for you to walk right into the blast?"

Right then, a dirt-caked monk called out from the depths of the pit: "Sect Leader! The soil on the eastern side has already been turned! Someone tunneled their way in from the other flank!"

The trap had been laid long before they even arrived.

Jin Guangyao spun on his heel and slammed a vicious, bare-knuckle punch straight into the side of the wooden coffin. His back was turned to the room, but everyone could see the violent, silent tremor wracking his shoulders.

Wei Wuxian tilted his head, smiling. "Jin-zongzhu, did it ever occur to you that while you were busy playing the mantis stalking the cicada, a golden oriole was already perching right above your head? The shadow that’s been trailing your every move might be sitting in the rafters right now, watching your every step. Then again... who's to say it's even human?"

A heavy roll of thunder rattled the roof tiles, drowning out the world under a torrential wall of rain. At the words not human, a flicker of pure, unadulterated terror breached Jin Guangyao's face.

Su She sneered, stepping in front of his master. "Wei Wuxian, save your pathetic ghost stories—"

Jin Guangyao raised a stiff right hand, cutting him off mid-sentence. The naked panic on his face vanished in an instant, forcibly smothered back into submission. "Save your breath for something useful. Clean your wounds. The moment I purge this poison from my veins, rally the remaining disciples. We move out immediately."

Su She hesitated. "Sect Leader, the prize they dug out...?"

Jin Guangyao’s lips were bloodless. "If it has been taken, it is gone. We cannot linger here any longer."

"Understood!"

Earlier, while trading blows with Fairy, Su She had taken several nasty gashes from the spiritual hound. His robes were shredded at the forearms and chest, the claw marks digging deep enough into the meat to bleed through his white tunic. Left untreated, the blood loss would leave him useless in a fight.

Jin Guangyao drew a paper packet of medicinal powder from his inner robe and tossed it over. Su She caught it with both hands, giving a curt nod. True to his orders, he didn't waste another breath on Wei Wuxian, turning his back to strip down his tunic and tend to his wounds.

Jin Guangyao, his left hand completely paralyzed by the toxic blister, sank onto the stone floor to focus on circulating his spiritual energy and burning out the poison. The surviving cultivators fanned out through the temple halls, keeping a tense, drawn-sword patrol. Watching those flashing steel edges, Nie Huaisang shrank further into his corner, his teeth chattering as he sneezed repeatedly into Lan Xichen’s robes, terrified that a stray blow might take his head off.

Watching the scene unfold, Wei Wuxian thought to himself: This Su She is an insufferable prick to everyone he meets, especially Lan Zhan. But when it comes to Jin Guangyao, he’s as loyal as an old dog.

His eyes drifted naturally toward Lan Wangji—only to catch a terrifying, razor-sharp chill flashing behind those pale eyes.

Lan Wangji’s voice cut through the cavernous hall like a crack of winter ice.

"Turn around."

Su She was busy dabbing medicinal powder over the bloody claw marks raked across his collarbone, his body angled sideways toward them. Hearing that cold, absolute command, his limbs moved on pure, subconscious instinct.

He turned.

The moment he faced the room, Jiang Cheng and Jin Ling's eyes snapped wide in horror.

The casual smirk on Wei Wuxian’s face died on the spot.

His voice came out a breathless, disbelieving whisper: "...It was you?!"


a/n- "螳螂捕蝉，黄雀在后" is "The mantis stalks the cicada, unaware of the oriole behind." This proverb means to pursue a narrow, immediate gain while completely neglecting a much greater danger

right behind you.
